To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

people with advanced cancer are likely to attend the ED because they have a fear that their symptoms will worsen, they have previously attended the ED, or because they are unsure of how to manage their symptoms in the community.

people with advanced cancer are likely to seek care in the ED when they feel anxious and/or unsafe at home, when they are unable to access other sources of care, and when they have a history of frequent ED use.
People with advanced cancer and caregivers often feel that the only safe place for them to go when they have a crisis is the ED.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the quality of care for people with advanced cancer at the end of life, and reducing the number of ED presentations by this population.
the need to improve the care of people living with advanced cancer, and to reduce the burden of ED care for those who are dying.
how to improve the care of patients with advanced cancer and how to reduce the burden on emergency services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
people with advanced cancer who attend the ED are a heterogeneous group with a range of reasons for attending.

the number of emergency department visits by people with an advanced cancer could be reduced with increased access to end-of-life symptom control, earlier collaboration between palliative care and oncology and increased access to community health care services.
the ED is not an appropriate place for the care of people with advanced and incurable cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decision-making process of patients and caregivers to attend the ED is complex.

the decision making processes for people with advanced cancer are complex, and that a better understanding of the factors that influence decision making could help reduce emergency department visits by this group.

patients with advanced cancer are often seeking emergency department (ED), not necessarily because their condition requires immediate attention but rather because they are not receiving adequate care in the community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people with advanced cancer want to feel that they are in safe hands.
the ED is not a safe place for people with advanced cancer at the end-of-life.
people with advanced cancer are often seeking reassurance and safety, and this should be considered when developing systems of care.
